core_themes.name: Scale and growth of fee charging
core_themes.claim: Tenant letting fees are widespread, have risen significantly in recent years, and vary considerably in amount across agents even for similar services.

core_themes.name: Lack of tenant control and market power imbalance
core_themes.claim: Because landlords, not tenants, appoint and pay agents' core incentives, tenants have little to no ability to negotiate, opt-out of, or exert competitive pressure on letting fees.

core_themes.name: Opacity and difficulty comparing fees
core_themes.claim: Variation in how agents display and itemise fees makes it difficult for tenants to understand, find, or compare charges across agents, undermining existing transparency rules.

core_themes.name: Financial and behavioural harm to tenants
core_themes.claim: High, repeated up-front fees create real financial hardship, deter mobility, risk homelessness, and make it harder for tenants to save for deposits or challenge rogue practices.

core_themes.name: Rebalancing market incentives toward landlords
core_themes.claim: Banning tenant fees shifts cost-bearing to landlords, who can shop around and negotiate, sharpening agents' incentives to compete on price and quality for landlord business.

core_themes.name: Improving tenant transparency and comparability
core_themes.claim: The ban lets tenants see the true, all-in cost of a property via the advertised rent alone, making it easier to compare properties and budget without hidden fees.

core_themes.name: Scope of the ban and limited carve-outs
core_themes.claim: The ban should cover all fees charged to tenants by agents, landlords or third parties (leaving only rent and a refundable deposit), with narrow exceptions such as holding deposits and tenant-caused charges, and should be accompanied by exploration of capping or easing deposit burdens.

core_themes.name: Likely effect on rents and overall cost
core_themes.claim: While some agent costs may be passed through to landlords and reflected in rents, this is expected to be fairer and more transparent than hidden up-front tenant fees, drawing support from the Scottish precedent where rent impacts were minimal.

core_themes.name: Enforcement through local Trading Standards
core_themes.claim: The ban will be enforced primarily by local authorities' Trading Standards, building on their existing role enforcing redress and transparency requirements.

core_themes.name: Tenant empowerment and education as a compliance tool
core_themes.claim: Educating and empowering tenants to challenge non-compliant agents, including via local authorities or the county court, will reduce reliance on proactive policing and aid enforcement.

core_themes.name: Strengthening enforcement infrastructure
core_themes.claim: Additional measures—such as a lead enforcement authority, increased data sharing, and wider regulation of the sector—are being explored to support and strengthen local enforcement of the ban.

core_themes.name: Penalties for non-compliance
core_themes.claim: Non-compliance should carry meaningful deterrent penalties, with options including civil fines (potentially up to £30,000) or criminal prosecution/banning orders, modelled on existing Housing and Planning Act 2016 powers.
